recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. Revisit only if a new work-group decision explicitly changes Meta.source's datatype, cardinality, or Provenance relationship.
issue_request: FHIR-14217 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core BaseResource, raised and applied for STU3, requesting source on Resource.meta as new normative content and noting it should be fully applied including the Resource.meta table of contents.
initial_application: Commit 7acde0ac43e83f7b9b7076269eac28735def62f8 added Meta.source to source/datatypes/meta.xml on 2017-11-23 as a 0..1 uri element. Commit 56226183c1cd1b8a31928471771de6c317ae4410 updated the Meta.source documentation after the 2017-12-18 vote. Current source/fhir.ini maps meta to the Resource page, and current source includes Meta.source in the datatype row, Resource narrative table, _source search parameter bundle, and search prose.
additional_context: The summary said source : url, but the initial implementation used uri and later final decisions preserved the uri-based, single-source model while clarifying scope. FHIR-20688 and FHIR-20906 clarified that Meta.source can correspond broadly to Provenance.entity.what or Provenance.agent.who; FHIR-20908 rejected 0..* cardinality; FHIR-17232 reused Meta.source for canonical-resource current-service guidance; FHIR-49878 clarified the definition from source system to data source. Related audit commits for FHIR-20688, FHIR-20906, FHIR-17232, and FHIR-49878 already exist on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already satisfies FHIR-14217, including the Resource.meta table and the _source search parameter surface, and changing the datatype or adding redundant prose would exceed the seed issue and later decisions.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that Meta.source is not limited to a source system and can be a broader source identifier.
Clarified the possible relationship between Meta.source and Provenance.agent.who or Provenance.entity.what.
Rejected changing Meta.source cardinality to 0..*, supporting the current 0..1 source.
Used Resource.meta.source for current authoritative-service guidance on canonical resources.
Clarified Meta.source scope and data-source wording for R6.
